column3: Immediate antecedent: du'a amid zulumat, najja, then a pledged response before 6:64's shirk.
Rashad offers a single directed route, a secondary counterpoint to the post-rescue turn toward shirk.
Allah as khaliq of kull shay' and sole ilah frames 6:64's rescue as leaving no functional share for shirk.
The question "where are those you associated" tests whether shirk has any presence when needed.
Sudden or open punishment supplies a danger setting but adds neither najja nor the turn to shirk.
A selective najja from severe 'adhab gives a narrative instance of extraction from karb.
Crisis du'a is directed to Allah alone, followed by kashf and forgetting the shirk objects.
Nida' answered by najja from al-karb al-'azim supplies a direct rescue-through-call parallel.
Uses yunji in a condemned person's imagined ransom, a boundary case rather than Allah's rescue in 6:64.
Creation from turab and human spread do not clarify rescue, karb, or shirk here.
Rejects calling what lacks benefit or harm and depicts reversal after huda, a secondary counterpart to post-rescue shirk.
The settling of each naba' gives only a distant confirmation horizon for the warning in this passage.
Confidence under Allah's encompassing knowledge contrasts with fear of associated powers.
Denial and the speaker's lack of wakala add little to 6:64's rescue-and-shirk sequence.
Generic takdhib by the transgressor does not add a usable route to 6:64.
Names shirk without sultan among grave prohibitions, sharpening the negative judgment at 6:64's close.
A bare statement of favor to Musa and Harun lacks the relevant rescue or shirk relation.
Tunjikum from painful 'adhab extends najja to a stated transition out of affliction.
The two forms of shafa'a and their shares do not clarify 6:64.
Noah's nida' and divine response prepare the later rescue narratives but add no karb or shirk detail.
Shirk follows zann rather than established knowledge; the contrast reading limits more elaborate route imagery.
One ilah and declared bara'a from shirk supply a direct doctrinal counterpoint to the final clause.
Accountability and reminder for the muttaqun do not materially develop 6:64.
A repeated family najja from al-karb al-'azim confirms the pattern but is redundant after 21:76.
Bara'a from the alleged alihah that can harm marks refusal of the rivals implicated by shirk.
Nasr and predominance add a broad outcome, not the rescue-and-association pattern.
Rejecting another wali and embracing islam frames shirk as divided allegiance, though only indirectly tied to karb.
A compact rescue-from-karb formula is corroborative but contextually thin and repetitive.
Prayer, taqwa, and return to Allah do not add to the specific sequence at 6:64.
Loss exposes a prior shirk relation; it supplies a later consequence rather than a rescue parallel.
Death by Allah's permission and recompense do not clarify 6:64.
Najjini after a request for decisive separation presents rescue as an outcome of judgment.
The opening warning against mockers has no focused link to 6:64.
Cosmic standing and later emergence from earth are not a rescue-and-shirk parallel.
Following wahy, affirming one ilah, and turning from mushrikun states the required opposite response.
Sea peril produces exclusive du'a; after najja to land, shirk returns, closely paralleling 6:64.
Origins and later creation do not materially illuminate the focus ayah.
Allah's knowledge of deviation and guidance gives a loose route frame only.
Shared punishment supplies a contrary endpoint for shared shirk, not the rescue mechanism.
Kufr despite Allah's self-sufficiency is a broad ingratitude parallel, secondary to shirk.
Noah and companions are saved in the ship, but this repeats the rescue narrative without the focus's turn.
Demanding that alleged shuraka' be produced tests the evidentiary emptiness of shirk.
Filling bellies from the tree adds no relevant relation.
A list of righteous figures does not clarify 6:64.
The descent with kull amr is not a usable rescue or shirk parallel.
Qul Allah amid dispute over the kitab is a remote source-authority support only.
Nasr for Nuh and drowning of deniers gives a broad narrative contrast without shirk's post-rescue reversal.
The collective prostration does not develop 6:64.
Najja from a former milla is followed by refusal to return, a durable alternative to 6:64's relapse into shirk.
A further list of favored figures adds no focused evidence.
Defines shirk as grave zulm, explaining the seriousness of 6:64's final accusation.
Bare turning away has no specific connection.
The servant's standing and the crowd's gathering do not clarify the focus.
Wages and divine witnessing are not a focused rescue or shirk relation.
Allah's standing over every nafs exposes the unsupported naming of shuraka' and their false authority.
Shirk renders deeds ineffective, supplying a consequential warning after the focus's accusation.
The gathering of skilled magicians has no relevant connection.
Trust and individual recompense do not develop 6:64.
The delayed sign and ineffective late iman are only a broad warning context.
Enclosure at sea, exclusive du'a, and a vow of shukr give a close crisis-rescue pattern, though later parallels are fuller.
Benefits of an'am do not clarify the focus.
Gifts to Bani Isra'il do not add a rescue-and-shirk relation.
The shared judgment scene does not materially illuminate 6:64.
The angel assigned to death and return to the Rabb use different agency and setting from 6:64's rescue.
Najja of believers marked by taqwa shows selective separation from ruin, though without the focus's shirk turn.
Commanded qist and exclusive ikhlas in du'a state a devotional counterpart to calling Allah in distress.
Allah's encompassing relation supports universal dependence only indirectly.
All shafa'a belonging to Allah is a secondary exclusivity support, not a rescue scene.
All beings belong to Allah and are qanituun, reinforcing the undivided allegiance contradicted by shirk.
Joy in fadl and rahma does not clarify 6:64's crisis sequence.
Creation of pairs and conveyances supplies no focused link.
After Allah removes durr, a group immediately commits shirk: the concise post-relief pattern of 6:64.
Najja from humiliating 'adhab gives another social-scale rescue instance, now largely redundant.
Ni'ma is from Allah and durr elicits crying only to Him, establishing the pre-relief dependence behind 16:54 and 6:64.
Membership and kin priority do not clarify the focus ayah.
Hanifiyyah and non-shirk state a general counterposition without rescue.
Selective najja of Salih and believers repeats the rescue pattern without the post-rescue test.
The direct prohibition of shirk fixes the normative boundary, without developing karb or najja.
The named exemplary figures do not add relevant evidence.
Najja from Pharaoh's coercive punishment illustrates collective release from an oppressive karb.
The prayer seeks najja from Pharaoh, his deed, and the unjust people, broadening rescue beyond one immediate threat.
The straight path and guidance offer only a distant contrast to the focus.
Provision's expansion and measure do not clarify rescue or shirk here.
Allah as Rabb of kull shay' makes seeking another rabb an incompatible authority claim, supporting the f02 exclusivity line.
The distinguishing of wise matters does not materially illuminate 6:64.
Creation, return, and provision are set against the challenge of another ilah, reinforcing exclusive divine capability.
Guidance joined to refusal of shirk supplies an affirmative response opposite to 6:64's relapse.
Sea-wave peril, exclusive du'a, and najja to land parallel the crisis scene; its varied aftermath is a secondary comparison.
The Pharaoh pattern and drowning do not add to 6:64 beyond a broad punitive contrast.
Praise after najja from unjust people gives a grateful response, but the rescue pattern is already well covered.
Iblis's expulsion for arrogance does not clarify the focus.
Claimed shuraka' fail to answer when called; this is boundary evidence for their uselessness in need.
Open paths through earth do not add a focused relation.
Multiple ilah would fragment creation and authority, a conceptual support for f02 rather than the rescue event.
The destroyed garden parable does not clarify 6:64.
The command to show added shuraka' subjects shirk to a direct capability challenge.
Mockery and wandering in rebellion do not add to the focus.
The value of the narratives is too general to clarify 6:64.
Allah's possession, rahma, and gathering give a broad authority frame but not the focus sequence.
The unequal allocation to Allah and shuraka' exposes shirk as an operative, one-way arrangement.
Najjaynakum from Pharaoh's people supplies an early collective rescue-from-'adhab parallel.
Sea crossing and Pharaoh's drowning repeat a rescue setting without the focus's shirk reversal.
Shirk without revealed sultan is linked to insecurity, a consequential boundary for 6:64's accusation.
The non-forgiveness of shirk fixes a grave doctrinal consequence of the focus's final clause.
A second explicit warning on shirk confirms its gravity, though it adds no rescue scene.
Association in worship is rejected directly but is redundant with closer shirk evidence.
The immediate preceding challenge asks who would be called under Allah's punishment or the Hour, directly preparing 6:41-64.
Ba'sa' and darra' sent to earlier communities establish an affliction setting meant to elicit tadarru'.
Failure to practice tadarru' under ba'sa' supplies a contrary response to the distress-call pattern.
Associating what lacks sultan is weighed against security under Allah, sharpening the fear and reliance question.
Iman unmingled with zulm is tied to security and huda, a secondary contrast to shirk after rescue.
The making of jinn as shuraka' shows the constructive act of association that 6:64 condemns.
Allah's non-wakala over their shirk marks a boundary of responsibility, not a rescue explanation.
The straight din and Ibrahim's non-shirk position provide the positive allegiance contrary to 6:64.
No partner for Him and commanded islam make explicit the undivided response absent in 6:64.
Najja of Hud and his companions, with the deniers cut off, gives a selective communal rescue parallel.
Najja of Lut and his family supplies another extraction from a corrupt community.
Najjaynakum from Pharaoh's people repeats release from severe imposed 'adhab.
A plea for a sound child introduces dependence in distress but not the focus's rescue-and-shirk structure.
After receiving what was requested, association follows; this is a distinct post-gift reversal parallel.
Those called besides Allah are servants like the callers, a capability boundary on shirk.
Those called besides Allah cannot help their callers or themselves, directly limiting crisis recourse.
Remembered shelter, support, and provision after vulnerability give a communal gratitude counterpoint.
Durr elicits du'a in every posture, then is forgotten when removed; a close reversal pattern without explicit shirk.
Claimed shafa'a through others is challenged before Allah, supplying a mediation form of shirk.
Do not call what cannot benefit or harm besides Allah directly defines the exclusive object of need.
When Allah touches durr none removes it but Him, providing a concise capability basis for 6:64.
After najja from sea peril, baghy follows; this preserves the post-rescue failure as a close secondary parallel.
The separation of worshippers from their shuraka' gives a later contrary outcome for association.
Najja of Nuh and the ship's companions repeats preservation through an overwhelming threat.
Divine nasr and rescue at an extremity of messenger distress are a broad, indirect parallel.
Other calls receive no answer, directly contrasting Allah as the sole effective addressee in crisis.
Bringing Musa's people out of zulumat and recalling Allah's days provides a collective release pattern.
The prohibition on taking two ilah states the undivided divine claim violated by shirk.
Denial after what Allah has given supplies a post-benefit reversal adjacent to 16:54's direct parallel.
Those besides Allah lack rizq capacity, constraining the practical claims behind shirk.
Those invoked besides Allah cannot remove or transfer durr, a direct capability boundary.
Sea distress makes all other invoked beings vanish; deliverance to land is followed by turning away.
Claims of alihah besides Allah require sultan, reinforcing the evidentiary boundary on shirk.
Allah has no partner in judgment, extending undivided authority beyond the rescue scene.
The garden-owner's lack of a supporting party besides Allah is a secondary failure-of-help parallel.
Najjaynakum from the enemy recalls a collective deliverance, though without the final shirk turn.
Ayyub's durr and his direct call to the Rabb provide a personal karb-and-du'a parallel.
Kashf of Ayyub's durr shows divine removal of affliction after the call.
Yunus calls from ghamm and receives response and najja, an especially close karb-rescue parallel.
Calling what cannot harm or benefit besides Allah names a futile alternative refuge.
Calling another ilah without burhan is condemned and denied success, direct contrary evidence for shirk.
Alleged gods lack creation and control over harm, benefit, death, life, and return.
Najja of those with iman and taqwa repeats selective preservation from a destructive outcome.
Answering the distressed caller and removing su' is immediately joined to the challenge of another ilah with Allah.
Claimed shuraka' neither answer the call nor can support their claim, a direct end-state boundary.
Durr produces turning and du'a to the Rabb; after rahma a group commits shirk, closely matching 6:64.
Acknowledgment that Allah created the heavens and earth exposes a tension with later association.
Those called besides Allah possess nothing and have no share, support, or effective intercession.
The alleged worship of others is exposed before the angels, a later accountability boundary for shirk.
Allah alone governs the cosmic order; alleged partners possess not even a qitmir.
Those called besides Allah cannot hear or answer, and will disown the association on the Day.
If al-Rahman intends durr, other alihah's shafa'a cannot avail or rescue the caller.
Taking alihah besides Allah in hope of nasr supplies a broad false-help parallel.
Calling Ba'l while leaving the best Creator offers a compact rival-call contrast.
Durr produces exclusive du'a; after ni'ma the caller forgets and sets up rivals to Allah.
Acknowledged divine creation sits beside calls to powerless others, a capability test for shirk.
The contrast between Allah alone and those besides Him records the divided response underlying shirk.
After durr, a ni'ma from Allah is reframed as personal knowledge, a secondary post-relief failure.
Allah alone is called and rejected, while association is accepted; it directly frames the opposed responses.
The call to najat is set against a call toward the Fire, giving a contrary route reading.
Human du'a after sharr and despair gives only a general distress background.
After rahma following durr, turning away supplies another post-relief reversal pattern.
Those called besides Allah do not hold shafa'a except under the stated condition, limiting rescue intermediaries.
None is more astray than one who calls besides Allah those who will not answer until the Day.
Taken alihah fail to help and disappear, an outcome boundary for false reliance.
The servant calls only the Rabb and associates none, the affirmative opposite of 6:64's final turn.
The caller has no power over durr or rashad, distinguishing agency from the sole Rabb addressed.
No one can protect from Allah and no refuge exists apart from Him, extending exclusive rescue dependence.
